items.line: The New York City mayor's account posts an 8-second video with no text, quoting Vice President JD Vance's "We got your back, New York!" photo post. The capture has no description of either, so what they show is not stated here.

Fox News reports that President Trump said in a Fox & Friends interview that the U.S. will end about $4 billion a year in aid to Israel by the end of the year, and that Benjamin Netanyahu agreed. Not checked here.
The account Political Polls lists new AtlasIntel Senate polls, among them Michigan with El-Sayed up 7 and Texas with Talarico up 6. It does not link the polls themselves. Not checked here.
VoteHub posts results for the Guam non-voting delegate race with all precincts reported: Alicia Anne Garrido Limtiaco 51.0 percent, James Craig Moylan 48.8 percent. Not checked here.
Pop Base says the U.S. has launched strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island the night before the midterm elections, with two photos. Not checked here.

Rahul Gandhi posts a video with text in Hindi and English, challenging Prime Minister Narendra Modi to a public debate on who is anti-national and on the US trade deal, the Adani case and Epstein. Nirmala Sitharaman replies that Parliament is the venue. Not checked here.
California Governor Gavin Newsom posts on Election Day that anyone who shows up to vote illegally will be tracked down, arrested and prosecuted. The post carries a link. Not checked here.
TMZ reports that Ethan Klein and his wife Hila are divorcing. The post links the story. Not checked here.
BBC News reports that the Alton Towers theme park in Staffordshire has closed its World of David Walliams area.
Bethesda posts a video for "The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel", inviting players to the next journey to Tamriel.

CD Tenerife announces, in Spanish, the death of its player Jesús de Miguel Alameda on Tuesday at 8:00 and asks for respect for his family's privacy. A related earlier post from Laliga News, in Spanish, links a clip it describes as a heavy blow to him in the match against Andorra. The club's post gives no cause.
Fabrizio Romano reports that Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel has died from the consequences of an incident in the club's match against FC Andorra. WBC24 says the club confirmed it. Not checked here.
Watcher.Guru, an aggregator, reports that investor Bill Ackman says the stock market has turned into a "casino." Not checked here.
yoxic says Kai Cenat showed his TikTok revenue after a 30-minute stream, in a 37-second video. Not checked here.
TMZ reports that Donald Trump says he will move to Israel to become prime minister if the U.S. turns on him. The post links TMZ's story. Not checked here.
Decision Desk HQ projects that Jon Ossoff wins the Georgia U.S. Senate general election, calling it at 7:18 PM EST. NBC News also projects an Ossoff win. Projections are not official results.

Adam Schefter reports, citing sources, that former Super Bowl champion quarterback Russell Wilson interviewed today for the head coaching job at North Carolina State, where he played three seasons. Schefter adds that Philip Rivers is also a prominent candidate. Not checked here.

The U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement account posts on Election Day that anyone who votes illegally will be found, arrested and prosecuted, and that there will be no escape. The post makes the statement and gives no case. Not checked here.
Dragan Maricic asks why the main Windows drive is called C: and what happened to A: and B:, calling it a dumb tech question. The post gives no answer.

Ian Rapoport reports, citing sources, that Arizona Cardinals running back Jeremiyah Love is headed to injured reserve with a high-ankle sprain that he says rules him out for four to five weeks. Not checked here.

CNN Breaking News says CNN projects that Democrats will retake control of both the House and the Senate, giving them power to check the White House for the last two years of Trump's term. The projection is CNN's. Not checked here.
The Democratic Party account says Virginia voters passed Question 2, repealing the 2006 same-sex marriage ban and codifying marriage equality. Not checked here.
SportsCenter posts a clip of Christian Bale talking about his upcoming role as Al Davis in the film "Madden", quoting Davis's motto, "Once a Raider always a Raider".
The NHL says the Jets stormed back from a 4-0 deficit in Montreal in only 2:06. The post has a clip.
Mark Gurman says iOS 27.2 is so buggy that he is not sure 27.3 could be worse, so trying it might be worth it, adding "Not a recommendation". Not checked here.

IGN reports that Dead by Daylight developer Behavior Interactive has apologized again and removed free items from a streamer's account, after a community staff member allegedly gifted the streamer every in-game item. The allegation is IGN's and has not been checked here.
Acyn, who posts political clips, shares a video he says shows Fox calling South Carolina for Annie Andrews, with Hannity reacting "Brutal." The post does not say which race. Not checked here.

OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman says people should always be in control of the future, that OpenAI rejects the idea that people should be relegated to doing what "AI systems think makes sense to reward in humans", and that this should limit AI progress.

Senator Bernie Sanders says Democrats will now control the House and Senate and be able to hold Trump accountable, and that "we must aggressively fight for working families." The count of seats is his statement and has not been checked here.
The account nicksortor says it looks like Republicans will likely lose a U.S. Senate seat in Mississippi, with over 95% of votes reporting, and that the race is not over. Not checked here.

The account infolibnews posts a video it says shows Mark Levin insisting he should not be blamed if Republicans lose the midterms and that the Iran war is not the reason. The capture has no description of the video. Not checked here.
The account FOS says former NFL sideline reporter Michele Tafoya lost her first political race, running as a Republican in Minnesota, and that several NFL team owners backed her. Not checked here.
The account kchartsmaster says JISOO will release an original song for 'The Angry Birds Movie 3'. The post links to a Hollywood Reporter article headed the same way; that has not been checked here.
Elon Musk posts: "Guess my election-interfering space lasers didn’t work this time", with a shrug emoji.
Abdul El-Sayed says he is headed to the U.S. Senate to serve Michigan, and that Michigan won together.
The account EndWokeness lists Texas results by group, which it attributes to an NBC exit poll, with Democratic and Republican margins for white, Latino and Black voters. Not checked here.
Rep. Nancy Mace says Republicans have Senate leader John Thune to thank for the SAVE America Act not passing and for not securing elections earlier.
Naval posts: "Greed can be satisfied. Envy, cannot."
The official Formula 1 account says its first interview with Kimi as F1 champion is on its YouTube channel, and calls him the newly crowned world champ.

Tencent's Hunyuan account announces Hy4, which it says is new with vision and firmly among the leading open models. The post says it was built responsibly, with cyber and biosecurity in mind. Not checked here.
The account AshCrypto posts a chart and says Bitcoin jumped $2,400 in the past 4 hours and bounced from support at the 50-week moving average.
The account BRICSinfo says Iran responded to the Democrats' wins in the U.S. elections with "Americans said NO TO WAR…And we endorse this message." It names no speaker. Not checked here.

State Rep. Angie Nixon posts a message to supporters in Florida, saying the result was not the one she fought for, that the movement will continue, and that she is not going anywhere. The post does not name the race. Not checked here.
Pop Crave, an entertainment and news aggregator, says Democrat Deb Haaland has won the New Mexico governor race and will be the first Native American woman to be a governor. Not checked here.
